findings.location: Star rating indicators under each book cover (e.g., 'A Light in the Attic')
findings.issue: The bright yellow used for filled stars and the very light grey used for unfilled stars have extremely low contrast against the white background, failing WCAG AA non-text contrast requirements (minimum 3:1).
findings.user_impact: Users with low vision or color vision deficiencies will struggle to determine the star ratings of the books.
findings.recommendation: Change the active star color to a darker amber/gold (e.g., #b57c00) and the inactive star color to a medium grey (e.g., #767676) to ensure they are clearly visible against the white background.

findings.location: Book titles below star ratings in the product grid (e.g., 'Sapiens: A Brief History ...')
findings.issue: Book titles are strictly truncated to a single line with ellipses. This cuts off crucial book information, making titles look repetitive and uniform, which disrupts visual scanning and hierarchy.
findings.user_impact: Users cannot see the full title of the books without navigating to the product page, reducing the scannability of the list.
findings.recommendation: Remove single-line truncation and use CSS line-clamp to allow titles to wrap up to 2 or 3 lines, ensuring a consistent height for all product cards.

findings.location: Sidebar category list on the left side of the page
findings.issue: The list of categories is extremely dense with minimal vertical spacing (line-height/padding) between items. This creates a dense, hard-to-read vertical block that contrasts poorly with the open spacing of the main grid.
findings.user_impact: Users with motor impairments or those on touch devices will find it difficult to accurately tap or click individual category links.
findings.recommendation: Increase the vertical padding of the sidebar list items to at least 8px (or a line-height of 1.6) to improve readability and target size, and consider adding collapsible categories to reduce the list length.
